questions.q: What are two of PL/SQL's built-in named exceptions mentioned in this lesson?
options: NO_DATA_FOUND and TOO_MANY_ROWS
SQLEXCEPTION and SQLWARNING
EXIT_HANDLER and CONTINUE_HANDLER
ERROR_MESSAGE and ERROR_NUMBER
questions.explain: NO_DATA_FOUND and TOO_MANY_ROWS are specific, named Oracle exceptions you can catch individually before falling back to WHEN OTHERS.

questions.q: What do SQLERRM and SQLCODE provide inside a PL/SQL exception handler?
options: The current error's message text and its numeric error code
The name of the table that caused the error
The line number where the error occurred
Nothing — they are not valid inside an exception handler
questions.explain: SQLERRM returns the error message text and SQLCODE the numeric error code, both usable inside any exception handler, including WHEN OTHERS.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe MySQL's error-handling model as a genuine ergonomics gap compared to TRY/CATCH or EXCEPTION blocks?
options: The handler is DECLAREd separately from the code it protects, rather than wrapping the risky code in a single TRY or block body
MySQL has no error handling capability at all
MySQL's handlers can only catch syntax errors
MySQL requires every query to be wrapped in XML
questions.explain: Unlike TRY/CATCH or an EXCEPTION block where the protected code and its handler are visually together, MySQL's DECLARE HANDLER is declared separately from the statements it protects, which many developers find less intuitive.

questions.q: What is the difference between MySQL's EXIT HANDLER and CONTINUE HANDLER?
options: EXIT HANDLER stops the current block when it fires; CONTINUE HANDLER resumes execution after the triggering statement
They are two names for the exact same behavior
EXIT HANDLER only works with cursors; CONTINUE HANDLER only works with SELECT
CONTINUE HANDLER stops the block; EXIT HANDLER resumes it
questions.explain: An EXIT HANDLER stops the enclosing block on firing, while a CONTINUE HANDLER lets execution resume after the statement that triggered it — the same CONTINUE HANDLER mechanism used for cursor 'not found' detection.

questions.q: How does PL/pgSQL's exception-handling syntax compare to PL/SQL's?
options: It is syntactically close to Oracle's model, using EXCEPTION WHEN condition THEN...WHEN OTHERS THEN...END, with SQLERRM for the message
PostgreSQL has no exception-handling mechanism at all
PL/pgSQL uses MySQL's DECLARE HANDLER model instead
PL/pgSQL requires TRY/CATCH exactly like T-SQL
questions.explain: PL/pgSQL's EXCEPTION WHEN...THEN...WHEN OTHERS...END block and its SQLERRM function closely mirror Oracle's PL/SQL exception model.
